precepts.text: Eight: Taberah. When the people complained, it displeased the Lord, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them; the same thing he is going to do in America. Nine: the lusting for flesh. We remember the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick; ungrateful, complaining about the manna of heaven.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number eight is Taberah. “And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the Lord burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.” More complaining, and the Most High started burning people with fire, the same thing he is going to do in America. “And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched.”

Then the lusting for flesh: “the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. Always about food; black people for you.

“But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes.” Ungrateful, complaining about the manna. Over and over the Lord was longsuffering, and over and over Moses prayed and the Lord pardoned, as Numbers 14:20 says: “I have pardoned according to thy word”.

precepts.text: And he called the name of that place Kibrothhattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number nine: the lusting for flesh ended in a graveyard. “And he called the name of that place Kibroth–hattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.” Taberah was number eight; Kibroth-hattaavah is number nine.

Number ten is the report of the spies, the doubt and fear of Numbers 13 and 14, and there the Most High had enough. “Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it”. Everyone twenty and upward fell in the wilderness, save Caleb and Joshua.

The Most High deals in numbers, and everything in the Bible is significant. Ten times he was longsuffering, and places like Kibroth-hattaavah still carry the names of what our fathers did.

precepts.text: Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things. That curse was also on us in ancient Egypt: we had to serve the Egyptians for the want of all things, the same way you have to serve for it today.
precepts.point: Guess what: it is the same thing with us here in America. A lot of you have food, you are full, you are comfortable. Well, for now.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
In the wilderness the children of Israel wept and said, “We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. What are they saying? Deuteronomy 28:48 explains it.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Serving our enemies in hunger and in thirst is one of the curses that was upon us, and it was also a curse that was on us in ancient Egypt. We had to serve the Egyptians for the want of all things. It is the same today: you need money to buy food, and you have to serve for it.

Back then we had fish, because the Nile was abundant in fish, and we had melons. So brothers got delivered from oppression and started talking about going back to Egypt: even though we were oppressed, at least there we had some good food. It is the same thing with us here in America. A lot of you have food, you are full, you are comfortable. Well, for now.

precepts.text: After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do. Why did God say that? Because we learned the Egyptian customs while we were there. The same way here in America you learned the names of the week, named after their gods; that is idolatry. Everything you learned in Egypt, forget it. It is going to be the same when we are delivered up out of here.
precepts.point: Guess what: it is the same thing with us here in America. A lot of you have food, you are full, you are comfortable. Well, for now.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
It was not just that the Egyptians fed us. Everything we learned, we learned from the Egyptians back then. So when we came out of Egypt, God said: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do”.

Why did God say not to do after the doings of Egypt? Because we learned the Egyptian customs while we were there, the Egyptian names of the week. It is the same way here in America: you talk about Monday and Tuesday and all of that, days named after their gods, and all that is idolatry.

So God says, everything you learned in Egypt, forget it. The people who longed for the fish and the melons of Egypt were still holding on to Egypt in their hearts. And it is going to be the same thing when we are delivered up out of here, out of spiritual Egypt: everything we learned from this land, we will have to leave behind.

precepts.text: We remember the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick; the people longed for Egypt in the wilderness.
precepts.point: So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

precepts.why:
God led Israel around the land of the Philistines, “Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt”. Israel would have been fearful at the sight of the Philistine army and turned back, because the people felt a false security in Egypt.

That false security shows itself in the wilderness. “We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. Out of bondage, they murmured for the food of Egypt: the fish, the leeks, the onions and the garlick. Egypt had fed them, and they longed for it.

The same spirit holds the people in America today: a little job, government assistance, a car, food from the store, and they never want this kingdom to come down. The Lord knew that spirit when he chose the road out of Egypt, and led the people about through the wilderness of the Red sea so they would not run back.

precepts.text: The ear of jealousy heareth all things; beware of murmuring, for the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.
precepts.point: Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.
precepts.why:
The Most High hates it when His people complain. He had just destroyed Egypt for Israel, its land, its infrastructure, its firstborn, and drowned its army in the sea, all to save the people out; then on the other side of the wilderness, at the first trial or tribulation, the people jumped off His bandwagon. “And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the Lord burnt among them.” The same is still being done to this day.

“Therefore he that speaketh unrighteous things cannot be hid: neither shall vengeance, when it punisheth, pass by him.” Vengeance, when it punisheth, does not pass by the murmurer; he receives the vengeance of the Lord, which is what the fire in the uttermost parts of the camp was.

“For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly: and the sound of his words shall come unto the Lord for the manifestation of his wicked deeds. For the ear of jealousy heareth all things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.” Nothing spoken behind closed doors is hidden. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly by the Lord and His angels, and the sound of a man's words comes unto the Lord, for the ear of jealousy heareth all things.

“Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.” The mouth that belieth, that slanders a brother, a sister, the leadership, or the Lord, slayeth the soul.

Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out. A problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.

precepts.text: The Lord holds council with His angels; that is the inquisition made into the counsels of the ungodly.
precepts.point: Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.
precepts.why:
The Lord “heard it” when the people complained, because nothing spoken is hidden from Him. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, by the Lord and His angels, and here is that council.

“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead? And one said on this manner, and another said on that manner.” The Lord holds council with His angels over the deeds of men; that is the inquisition made into the counsels of the ungodly.

So when the people complained in the uttermost parts of the camp, the sound of their words came unto the Lord, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them.

precepts.text: A mixed multitude of other nations went up with Israel out of Egypt.
precepts.point: They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.
precepts.why:
“And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting.” Who were they? “And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.” The mixed multitude were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel, who went up with the people out of Egypt.

It was not Israel complaining at first; it was the nations lusting after the food of Egypt, and “the children of Israel also wept again.” Gullible and assimilated as always, Israel followed right after them and murmured against their God.

The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it.

precepts.text: The strangers sojourning among Israel were to be their bondmen and bondmaids.
precepts.point: They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.
precepts.why:
The mixed multitude that fell a lusting were the other nations among Israel, and the law tells what they were for. “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids. Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.”

The strangers sojourning among Israel were to be the bondmen and bondmaids of Israel. Instead, the nations sprinkled in the camp led the lusting, and the children of Israel followed the very people they were to rule over, and wept for the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic of Egypt.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.
precepts.point: They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.
precepts.why:
They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing: they wept for what they ate freely in Egypt, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun. It is the same now with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.

precepts.text: Manna was angels' food, agreeing to every taste and tempering itself to every man's liking.
precepts.point: The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.
precepts.why:
“And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium”, gathered, ground, baked in pans, “and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil.” Read precept upon precept to understand what they despised.

“Instead whereof thou feddest thine own people with angels’ food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.” Manna is angels' food, the food the Lord feeds the angels, sent from heaven prepared without their labour; they only had to pick it up when it fell with the dew in the night.

“For thy sustenance declared thy sweetness unto thy children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.” It was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for.

To complain about that provision was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.

precepts.text: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit before his master was taken from him.
precepts.point: It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.
precepts.why:
The Lord “took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.” The same thing happened with Elijah and Elisha.

Elisha was Elijah's right hand and disciple. Before Elijah was taken up, “Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.” The spirit that was on the master passed to the disciple, as the spirit that was on Moses passed to the elders.

precepts.text: The sons of the prophets saw it and said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha.
precepts.point: It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.
precepts.why:
When the spirit of Moses rested on the seventy elders, they prophesied. When the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha, it could be seen too: “And when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.” They saw Elisha smite Jordan with the mantle and knew whose spirit was on him.

It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.

precepts.text: John forbade one casting out devils in Christ's name because he followed not with them, and Christ said, Forbid him not, for he that is not against us is for us.
precepts.point: The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.
precepts.why:
Joshua the son of Nun said, “My lord Moses, forbid them”, when Eldad and Medad prophesied in the camp. Moses answered, “Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!” Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it.

The apostles had the same spirit. “And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us. And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.” John wanted to forbid a man because he was not in their company, as Joshua wanted to forbid the two in the camp; Christ answered like Moses did.

The Most High wants all His people to be prophets. The lesson today is the same: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

precepts.text: When the Samaritans would not receive Him, James and John wanted to call down fire; Christ rebuked them, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of, for the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them.
precepts.point: The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.
precepts.why:
Moses asked Joshua, “Enviest thou for my sake?” Joshua did not know what spirit he was speaking from, and neither did James and John.

When Christ sent messengers into a village of the Samaritans and “they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem”, James and John said, “Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did? But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.”

Christ rebuked the wrong spirit in His disciples as Moses rebuked the envy in his young man. The man of God corrects the spirit, and the Lord's people are to be prophets, not enviers.

precepts.text: Be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats bringeth sickness, and by surfeiting many have perished.
precepts.point: The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, but the lesson also stands in nature: excess of meat brings sickness. Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence.
precepts.why:
The Lord gave them quails two cubits high round about the camp, and “while the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled against the people, and the Lord smote the people with a very great plague”, exactly as He had warned. The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, and the place was called Kibrothhattaavah, the graves of lust, “because there they buried the people that lusted.”

The lesson also stands in nature. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler. By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.”

Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence. Excess of meat brings sickness, and by surfeiting many have perished, as they perished at the graves of lust.

precepts.text: The people gathered the manna and ground it in mills, or beat it in a mortar, and made cakes of it.
precepts.point: Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
What is the millstone? A tool for grinding meal. “And the people went about, and gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in a mortar, and baked it in pans, and made cakes of it”. The manna was gathered and ground in mills or beaten in a mortar and baked into cakes; that is the work of the nether and the upper millstone.

No man shall take the millstone to pledge, “for he taketh a man’s life to pledge”: take the mill, and the man cannot grind his meal or make his bread.

precepts.text: Moses' grief: wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant, the burden of all this people is too heavy for me; kill me, I pray thee, and let me not see my wretchedness.
precepts.point: Israel became a burden to Moses to the point he asked the Most High to kill him rather than let him see his own wretchedness. While I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

precepts.why:
Israel became such a burden to Moses that he asked the Most High to kill him: “Wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant? and wherefore have I not found favour in thy sight, that thou layest the burden of all this people upon me? Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father beareth the sucking child”. They wept to him for flesh to eat, and “I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.”

Then: “And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness.” That is the grief of forty years with a stiffnecked people. When Moses says “I know thy rebellion, and thy stiff neck”, he knew it well enough to have begged for death rather than see his own wretchedness under it.

precepts.text: In the wilderness Joshua was the servant of Moses, one of his young men, his protege; those were his humble beginnings.
precepts.point: Joshua is called Moses' minister because when Moses was the leader, Joshua was the one always cleaving to him. He was not close to Moses in age; he was one of the young men that cleaved unto his elder, and if Moses was a good leader, beloved among the children of Israel, who better to rise up in his stead than the man who has his spirit?

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Joshua is called “Moses’ minister” because when Moses was the leader, Joshua was the one always cleaving to him. In the wilderness he was “Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men”. That was his protege; those were his humble beginnings.

He was not close to Moses in age; he was one of the young men that cleaved unto his elder. And if Moses was a good leader, beloved among the children of Israel, who better to rise up in his stead than the man who has his spirit?

precepts.text: The mixed multitude fell a lusting, and Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic of Egypt; comfortable in their oppression.
precepts.point: The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”.

That is the milk and honey of Egypt, the food they wept for. They were comfortable in their oppression and did not understand they were not free, in the house of bondage crying for its fish and cucumbers. It is the same mindset among our people in captivity today who say they are free and living their best life. These are the men of war who obeyed not the voice of the Lord and were consumed in the wilderness.

You cannot make this stuff up.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: I know what you are saying: if I was there I would never complain. Oh yes, you would. You would do exactly the same thing. Some of us will say the same thing when Christ brings us back into the wilderness: I remember the fast food. We hear the complaints every year at the Feast of Tabernacles: you do not like where your tent spot is, some bring AC and flat screens out to the wilderness. The Lord hears your murmuring in your tents.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick. Brothers got delivered from oppression and started talking about going back to Egypt, because at least there they had good food. The Nile was abundant in fish.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

points: After the plagues, the mockery of every god of Egypt and the sea split, Israel said we remember the fish we ate in Egypt freely, the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic. From Goshen we watched Egypt get jammed up and still wanted the fish.

That is the complainer among us today: I remember my Whopper and my Chick-fil-A, why must we be enemies with the good white man who gave me a job slinging fries. Our soul is dried away because nobody is dictating to us any more; why can't I have the EBT and sit on the couch.

And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: How black people are with food. We cannot do anything without food. It was not the bitter hard bondage that we remembered. It was the leeks, the onions, the garlic, the cucumbers. That is what we remembered from being in slavery under Egypt. That is what we remember from our time in Egypt — how good the food was.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes. You know what that is called, when your eyes are not satisfied or content with the things that the Lord has given you? That is called covetousness.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: The Most High hates it when His people complain. He had just destroyed Egypt for Israel, its land, its infrastructure, its firstborn, and drowned its army in the sea, all to save the people out; then on the other side of the wilderness, at the first trial or tribulation, the people jumped off His bandwagon, and the same is still being done to this day.

The Lord heard the complaining, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them. Vengeance, when it punisheth, does not pass by him that speaketh unrighteous things; the murmurer receives the vengeance of the Lord.

Nothing spoken behind closed doors is hidden. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, by the Lord and His angels, the same council seen when the Lord asked who shall persuade Ahab that he may fall at Ramothgilead; the sound of a man's words comes unto the Lord, for the ear of jealousy heareth all things.

Beware of murmuring and refrain the tongue from backbiting, for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought, and the mouth that belieth, that slandereth a brother, a sister, the leadership, or the Lord, slayeth the soul.
Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.
The people cried unto Moses, and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched; the Most High quenched the fire because Moses prayed on behalf of the children of Israel.
The place was called Taberah, because the fire of the Lord burnt among them.

The mixed multitude that fell a lusting were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel, the mixed multitude that went up with the people out of Egypt; the law in Leviticus tells what they were for, to be the bondmen and bondmaids of Israel.

It was not Israel complaining at first; it was the nations lusting after the food of Egypt, and the children of Israel, gullible and assimilated as always, followed right after them and murmured against their God. The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it.

They wept for the fish they ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. It is the same today with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out.
The manna was as coriander seed, the colour of bdellium; the people gathered it, ground it, baked it in pans, and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil.

The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.
Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent; the anger of the Lord was kindled greatly, and Moses also was displeased.

The people Moses bore are the same people today; this teaching identifies the children of Israel with the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native American Indians, and the sheer rebellion and complaining in these chapters is one of the marks of the people.

Moses asked the Most High why He had afflicted His servant and laid the burden of all this people on him: have I conceived all this people, that thou shouldest say, Carry them in thy bosom as a nursing father? He was carrying grown people who acted like children.
Moses said, If thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand; he would rather die than bear so rebellious a people alone and look upon his own wretchedness.
The Lord told Moses to gather seventy men of the elders of Israel to the tabernacle, and He would take of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon them, that they bear the burden of the people with him.

Leadership works the same way today. The spirit on the head, the willingness to put in work, the humility, the patience, is meant to trickle down to the men below him, and the spirit the lead sisters roll in sets the spirit of the sisters in the congregation. That is why the leaders must be right according to the scriptures, because the Most High takes their spirit and lets it come upon the others.
The Lord said, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, It was well with us in Egypt, therefore the Lord will give you flesh.

Not one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty days, but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils and it be loathsome unto you. He fed them so much of the flesh they begged for that they would grow sick of it and hate it.
The reason for the judgment is stated plainly: because ye have despised the Lord which is among you. They spoke evil of His manna and wept to go back among the oppressors He had just destroyed.

Moses inquired how it could be done: the people are six hundred thousand footmen, and that count is not including women and children; there were millions in the wilderness. Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, or all the fish of the sea gathered together for them, to suffice them?

The Lord answered, Is the LORD'S hand waxed short? The One who destroyed Egypt asks whether His hand is short; thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not. Be patient and watch the word come to pass.
It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.

Moses gathered the seventy elders round about the tabernacle, and the Lord came down in a cloud and took of the spirit that was upon Moses and gave it unto the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.

Two of the men, Eldad and Medad, remained in the camp, and the spirit rested upon them, and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua the son of Nun said, My lord Moses, forbid them.

Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD'S people were prophets. Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it; the Most High wants all His people to be prophets.

The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

A wind from the Lord brought quails from the sea and let them fall by the camp, a day's journey on this side and on the other, two cubits high upon the face of the earth, and the people gathered them.

While the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled and He smote the people with a very great plague, exactly as He had warned. The place was called Kibrothhattaavah, the graves of lust, because there they buried the people that lusted.
